plan: For capital preservation, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
This approach prioritizes stability and a large cash buffer.
conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly reduces overall portfolio risk and potential drawdown by eliminating leveraged positions and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility but also limited upside.

plan: To balance risk and growth, sell all 2x and 3x leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Buy SPXS at 4% to add some inverse market exposure, balancing the portfolio.
This plan maintains a cash buffer and reduces overall concentration.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5% per month. It reduces leverage and concentration while introducing a small inverse position for hedging. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a focus on sustainable growth.

plan: For aggressive growth, trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name mandate.
Buy SPXS at 6% and NVDD at 6% from the scanner's best setups.
Add to SOXL and SPAL, targeting 5% each, to increase leveraged exposure.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for higher potential returns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4% per month by leveraging high-scoring scanner setups and increasing exposure to leveraged ETFs. This approach significantly raises both potential upside and drawdown risk. Be aware of daily decay and rebalancing effects of leveraged ETFs, and maintain strict stop discipline to manage potential rapid losses.

plan: For income generation, sell all high-beta and leveraged positions (METU, MSFU, SOXL, PLTU, SPAL, MUU) to zero.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the single-name mandate.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to increase exposure to income-generating assets.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month by rotating into income-focused ETFs and broad index exposure. It significantly reduces growth-oriented and leveraged positions for lower drawdown and more reliable distributions. Remember that distributions are variable and NAV can still decline in market downturns; this is not a savings account.
